Questions.question: Where was Ashan standing during the mistake?
What time did Ashan’s mistake take place?
What caused Ashan’s incorrect measurement?
Questions.answer: He read the scale too fast.
options: He read the scale too fast.
He switched off the reading too fast.

Questions.question: Why did Meena’s biscuits come out uneven?
options: She rotated them, but not at the right time.

activity_b.text: Ashan and Meena walked up to Ms. Perera after the morning briefing.
They looked a bit worried, and Ashan spoke first.
Good morning, Madam, we need to talk to you.
We realised we made some mistakes last week, and we want to discuss them with you.
Ayubowan, both of you. Thank you for coming forward.
Let’s go through them one by one.
Ashan, tell me then , what happened?
I put the wrong amount of flour into the bun mixture.
Where exactly were you when it happened?
I was near the steam kettle, close to the portioning scale.
And when did it happen? What time was it?
It was Wednesday, around a quarter past ten, just before the quality-check round.
Alright. Now tell me—how did you end up putting the wrong measurement into the mixture?
Madam… I read the scale too fast.
I should have calibrated it first, but I didn’t.
I usually check the scale, but not every day—maybe three times a week.
And why didn’t you calibrate it that morning?
Honestly, Madam, I thought it was still fine from the day before.
But now I know I shouldn’t assume that.
Good. So how are you going to make sure that it doesn’t happen again?
I’m going to calibrate the scale every morning and note the reading in the logbook.
I’m also going to slow down when reading measurements.
Alright. Now, Meena, what was your mistake?
The first batch of biscuits we made on Friday turned out very uneven.
Where were you when your mistake happened?
I was near the industrial oven, right beside the stainless-steel rack.
And when was that?
Friday around 2.00 p.m., during the first biscuit batch.
And how did your biscuits turn out so uneven?
Madam, I set the oven temperature correctly, but I placed the trays on different levels and I didn’t rotate them.
I also used the old blender for mixing, and the texture became slightly uneven.
Why didn’t you rotate the trays?
I was trying to save time, Madam.
I rotate them most of the time, but this time I was in a hurry.
So, how are you going to avoid these problems next time?
I’m going to follow the standard baking sequence, rotate trays after 5 minutes, and I might go through my notes on baking.
I’ll also check the blender blades before using it again.
Good. These are small mistakes, not disasters, but they matter.
Let’s stay consistent this week.
